prs.author: Genmin
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode was rejecting requests whose Accept header lists only 'application/json' (without also listing 'text/event-stream'), returning a 406 error. Both PRs relax the Accept-header validation in the same function (WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport request handling in src/server/webStandardStreamableHttp.ts) so JSON-only Accept headers are accepted in JSON response mode. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode was rejecting requests whose Accept header lists only 'application/json' (without also listing 'text/event-stream'), returning a 406 error. Both PRs relax the Accept-header validation in the same function (WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport request handling in src/server/webStandardStreamableHttp.ts) so JSON-only Accept headers are accepted in JSON response mode. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1996 adds a dedicated acceptsMediaType() parser that follows RFC 7231 Accept-header semantics: it splits on commas for multiple media ranges, strips whitespace/case, parses q-values and excludes entries with q=0, and compares type/subtype pairs (supporting wildcards) rather than doing a raw substring match. #2046's diff shows a simpler `acceptHeader?.includes('application/json')` / `.includes('text/event-stream')` check, which does not exclude q=0 (explicitly-rejected) media types and is vulnerable to substring false-positives on parameterized or extended media types (e.g. a subtype like 'application/json-seq' would satisfy `.includes('application/json')` even though it isn't a match). #1996's approach handles more of the edge cases the same underlying bug report implies without regressing correctness.

members.cluster_pick_reason: #1996 adds a dedicated acceptsMediaType() parser that follows RFC 7231 Accept-header semantics: it splits on commas for multiple media ranges, strips whitespace/case, parses q-values and excludes entries with q=0, and compares type/subtype pairs (supporting wildcards) rather than doing a raw substring match. #2046's diff shows a simpler `acceptHeader?.includes('application/json')` / `.includes('text/event-stream')` check, which does not exclude q=0 (explicitly-rejected) media types and is vulnerable to substring false-positives on parameterized or extended media types (e.g. a subtype like 'application/json-seq' would satisfy `.includes('application/json')` even though it isn't a match). #1996's approach handles more of the edge cases the same underlying bug report implies without regressing correctness.

clusters.pick_reason: #1996 adds a dedicated acceptsMediaType() parser that follows RFC 7231 Accept-header semantics: it splits on commas for multiple media ranges, strips whitespace/case, parses q-values and excludes entries with q=0, and compares type/subtype pairs (supporting wildcards) rather than doing a raw substring match. #2046's diff shows a simpler `acceptHeader?.includes('application/json')` / `.includes('text/event-stream')` check, which does not exclude q=0 (explicitly-rejected) media types and is vulnerable to substring false-positives on parameterized or extended media types (e.g. a subtype like 'application/json-seq' would satisfy `.includes('application/json')` even though it isn't a match). #1996's approach handles more of the edge cases the same underlying bug report implies without regressing correctness.
